newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Kuala Lumpur shares up 2.01 pct on blue chip rise.
newsitem.headline: Kuala Lumpur shares up 2.01 pct on blue chip rise.

text.p: A rise in blue chip shares boosted the key Kuala Lumpur Composite Index by 2.01 percent in late morning trading.
At 0309 GMT, the index was up 20.15 points to 1,021.70.
After a slow start this morning, the steady ringgit and downtrending interest rates bolstered sentiment in stocks, dealers said.
Others said there were small buying orders from local and foreign funds.
The ringgit was stalled around last week's levels in early Monday trading.
At the 0300 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate was fixed by interbank market players at 9.12 percent, extending last week's softening trend.
"Everyone is talking about Bank Negara adopting the right strategy, pushing interest rates down and letting the ringgit find its own level," said an institutional dealer at a local firm.
"I heard there's local funds buying," said an equity salesman at a Japanese brokerage in Singapore.
Another Singapore-based dealer said there were foreign buy programs in the market.
Some dealers half-jokingly attributed the sudden rise to the imminent return from a two-month holiday of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad on Tuesday.
Dealers note that the stock market seems to perform poorly when Mahathir is away.
"Mahathir is coming back and the market is welcoming him," said a dealer at a Penang-based brokerage.
